environment.status: Geometry-screened candidate; airflow and robot comparison not yet executed
environment.design_note: Two monitoring bays in the west, separated by a staggered column cluster with multiple passages. The eastern yard contains reachable service aisles but no monitoring target. All free-space cells retain clarity dynamics. A zero background target is an explicit task definition, as in Scenario 3, not a method-specific cost or exclusion. All methods begin with the same spatial unknown-wind prior over the complete environment.

wind_design.status: Intended placement only; no interior velocity field has been generated

task_passage.intent: Oppose B-to-A transit through the short diagonal gap; retain a physically traversable alternative around the western column.

remote_yard.intent: Spatially varying flow in the eastern service aisles, irrelevant to the short monitoring alternatives but included in global learning.

boundary_proposal.note: Physical boundary-condition proposal for a covered inspection yard. Inlet vectors must be normalized by the CFD setup. All other boundaries remain no-slip. Peak inlet speeds are not robot-plane wind speeds. These ports have not been simulated.

wind_design.acceptance_targets: At the robot plane: substantial opposing wind in the short gap (target opposing component 2.6–3.1 m/s, i.e. negative projection along B-to-A), a traversable weaker-wind western alternative, and low wind in A/B. Verify numerically; reject or revise the physical ports if these conditions do not arise. No interior clamping. Remote wind should not make global learning fail solely through collision.
wind_design.generation: Use the existing 3-D D3Q19 MRT / Smagorinsky solver and a frozen stationary vector mean. Configure physical boundary inlets/outlets and verify the resulting passage flow; never paint, mask or rescale interior velocities.
wind_design.information: Neither intended wind zone, true velocity nor support mask is supplied to POAM, acquisition, MBD or RPCBF.
